blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models leverage pretrained vision-language representations for instruction-conditioned robot control, yet their understanding of task-relevant 3D relations and how these relations evolve during manipulation remains largely implicit. To address this challenge, we introduce \textbf{WeaveVLA}, a framework that enhances VLA action generation by explicitly modeling task-relevant relative 3D relations and maintaining relational context across observations. WeaveVLA employs a task-conditioned sparse graph neural network to encode relative 3D relations among objects, the gripper, and nearby references. Pair-specific recurrent edge states integrate geometric evidence across observations to maintain evolving spatial context. A learned-query readout summarizes the updated graph representations into compact relational tokens, which condition the action expert alongside the original vision-language context. An auxiliary geometry reconstruction objective further encourages spatial structure preservation. We instantiate WeaveVLA on StarVLA-GR00T and $π_{0.5}$, achieving over 98\% average success on LIBERO with both backbones. On LIBERO-Plus, WeaveVLA improves success from 74.9\% to 82.0\% and from 85.7\% to 87.8\%, respectively, with additional improvements on CALVIN D$\rightarrow$D. On three real-world tasks, the StarVLA-GR00T-based variant improves average success from 55.6\% to 70.0\% under standard conditions and from 33.3\% to 53.3\% under OOD perturbations, surpassing the $π_{0.5}$ baseline in both settings.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models combine pretrained vision-language representations with robot demonstrations to learn instruction-conditioned manipulation policies.
Representative approaches such as OpenVLA and OpenVLA-OFT have advanced general-purpose manipulation, while recent systems have expanded these capabilities across robotic embodiments Kim et al. (2024) ; Kim et al. (2025) ; NVIDIA (2026) .
Flow-based policies, including π 0 \pi_{0} , π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} , and π 0.7 \pi_{0.7} , further advance continuous action generation, generalization, and steerable control Black et al. (2025b) ; Black et al. (2025a) ; Physical Intelligence et al. (2026) .
Despite these advances, understanding and maintaining the spatial relationships that govern manipulation remains an important challenge.
blocks.zh:
视觉-语言-动作(VLA)模型将预先训练的视觉-语言表现与机器人演示相结合来学习有指导条件的操控政策.
OpenVLA和OpenVLA-OFT等具有代表性的方法已经推进了通用操纵,而最近的系统则将这些能力扩展到了机器人的上层 Kim等 (2024); Kim等 (2025); NVIDIA (2026).
基于流动的政策,包括 ^ 0\pi_{0}, ^ 0.5\pi_{0.5}和 ^ 0.7\pi_{0.7}, 进一步推进连续动作生成,通化,并可引导控制 Black 等 (2025b) ; Black等 (2025a); 物理智能等 (2026).
尽管取得了这些进展,但了解和维持制约操纵的空间关系仍然是一个重大挑战。

blocks.en:
Robot actions depend on different relative 3D relations at different stages of manipulation. For example, placing a cup into a bowl requires reasoning about gripper–cup relations during grasping and cup–bowl relations during placement, while other object pairs may be less relevant.
These relations change with robot and object motion, while geometric estimation errors, viewpoint changes, and occasional occlusion can make their current configurations difficult to determine reliably Peng et al. (2026) .
SpatialVLA and 3DS-VLA improve spatial awareness through geometric representations and sequential spatial constraints Qu et al. (2025) ; Li et al. (2025) . GraphCoT-VLA and TriRelVLA further explore structured 3D relations for manipulation Huang et al. (2026) ; Zhou et al. (2026) .
This raises a central question: How can VLA models explicitly model task-relevant 3D relations and continuously update their representations as manipulation unfolds to support action generation?
blocks.zh:

这些关系随着机器人和物体运动而变化,而几何估计出错,观点变化,以及偶而被隔离,则可能使其当前配置难以可靠地确定彭等 (2026).
SpaceVLA和3DS-VLA通过几何表达和相继的空间约束来提高空间意识. Qu等 (2025); Li等 (2025). GraphCoT-VLA和TriRelVLA进一步探讨结构化的三维关系来操控黄等 (2026);周等 (2026).
这就提出了一个中心问题: VLA模型如何在操控过程中明确模拟与任务相关的三维关系并不断更新其表述以支持动作生成?

blocks.en:
To address this challenge, we introduce WeaveVLA , a framework that explicitly models task-relevant relative 3D relations and their evolution during manipulation to enhance VLA action generation, as illustrated in Fig. 1 .
Its object-centric representation combines visual features with estimated 3D geometry, using the robot’s tool center point (TCP) to anchor gripper–object relations.
A task-conditioned graph connects instruction-relevant objects, the gripper, and nearby spatial references, while edge-aware graph attention encodes their relative 3D geometry.
To maintain evolving spatial context, WeaveVLA assigns a recurrent state to each selected entity pair and updates it with valid geometric evidence across observations.
The resulting relation features are conditioned on the vision-language context and summarized into compact relational tokens. An auxiliary geometry reconstruction objective further encourages the learned relational features to preserve spatial structure.
Together with the original vision-language representations, these tokens condition a continuous action expert for robot manipulation.
blocks.zh:
为了应对这一挑战,我们引入了WeaveVLA,如图1所示,这个框架明确模拟与任务相关的相对三维关系及其在操纵过程中的演变,以加强VLA行动生成。
它的以物体为中心的表现结合了视觉特征和估计的3D几何,利用机器人的工具中心点(TCP)来锁定抓取对象关系.
以任务为条件的图表连接了指令相关对象,抓取器,以及相邻的空间参考,而边缘感知到的图表注意力则编码了相对的3D几何.
为了保持不断变化的空间上下文,WeaveVLA为每个选定的实体配对分配一个常态并用有效的几何证据进行跨观测更新.
由此产生的关系特征以视觉语言背景为条件,并归纳为紧凑的关系符号。 一个辅助几何重建目标进一步鼓励所学的关联特征来保护空间结构.
与最初的视觉-语言表达方式一起,这些符使机器人操纵的连续动作专家成为条件.

blocks.en:
We instantiate WeaveVLA on two VLA backbones, StarVLA-GR00T and π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} , and evaluate its effectiveness on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and CALVIN Mees et al. (2022) .
On the four standard LIBERO suites, WeaveVLA achieves average success rates of 98.3% and 98.2%, respectively, improving both backbones.
On LIBERO-Plus, it improves StarVLA-GR00T from 74.9% to 82.0% and π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} from 85.7% to 87.8%, demonstrating consistent gains across the two architectures.
On CALVIN D → \rightarrow D, WeaveVLA increases the average completed sequence length from 3.645 to 3.910 for StarVLA-GR00T, surpassing the original π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} baseline, and from 3.885 to 3.997 for π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} .
Across three real-world tasks, the StarVLA-GR00T-based WeaveVLA achieves average success rates of 70.0% under standard conditions and 53.3% under perturbations, outperforming both baselines.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows: 1. We introduce WeaveVLA, a 3D relational grounding framework that explicitly models task-relevant spatial relations among objects, the gripper, and nearby references to enhance VLA action generation. 2. We develop pair-specific recurrent relational updating to maintain evolving 3D relations across observations, integrating valid geometric evidence while preserving historical relational context. 3. We demonstrate consistent improvements across two VLA backbones on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and CALVIN D → \rightarrow D, and validate WeaveVLA on three real-world manipulation tasks, outperforming both baselines under standard and OOD conditions.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Vision-Language-Action Models
blocks.zh: 2.1 远景-语言-行动模式

blocks.en:
Building on pretrained vision-language representations and robot demonstrations, vision-language-action (VLA) research has advanced toward more generalizable robot manipulation.
Early approaches such as RT-2 and OpenVLA demonstrated the transfer of visual-semantic knowledge to robotic control Brohan et al. (2023) ; Kim et al. (2024) . OpenVLA-OFT improved action generation efficiency through continuous action representations, parallel decoding, and action chunking Kim et al. (2025) .
Subsequent VLA architectures further advanced continuous action generation and manipulation across diverse tasks Black et al. (2025b) ; Bjorck et al. (2025) ; Pan et al. (2026) . More recent models have expanded generalization and adaptability, with π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} demonstrating generalization to unseen environments Black et al. (2025a) and π 0.7 \pi_{0.7} advancing steerable execution and compositional generalization Physical Intelligence et al. (2026) .
LingBot-VLA 2.0 and GR00T N1.7 further advanced cross-embodiment manipulation Wu et al. (2026) ; NVIDIA (2026) , while Gemini Robotics 2 extended generalist control to whole-body and dexterous manipulation.
WeaveVLA complements these advances by augmenting VLA action generation with explicit, task-relevant 3D spatial relations.
blocks.zh:
在经过预先训练的视觉语言表现和机器人演示的基础上,视觉语言动作(VLA)的研究已经向更通俗的机器人操纵迈进.
RT-2和OpenVLA等早期方法展示了视觉语义知识被转移到机器人控制 Brohan等(2023年); Kim等(2024年). OpenVLA-OFT通过连续的动作表示,并平行地解码,和动作分解出Kim等(2025),提高了动作生成效率.
随后的VLA架构进一步推进了跨越不同任务的连续行动生成和操纵 Black等 (2025b); Bjorck等 (2025); Pan等 (2026). 较近期的模型扩展了通俗化和适应性, 显示通俗化到看不见的环境 Black等人(2025a)和 ^ 0.7\pi_{0.7}推进可导行执行和组成通论 物理智能等 (2026).
LingBot-VLA 2.0和GR00T N1.7进一步推进了交叉化操纵 Wu等 (2026); NVIDIA (2026),而双子机器人2则将通论控制扩展到了全身和自相残杀的操纵.
WeaveVLA通过以明确、与任务相关的3D空间关系增强VLA行动生成,来补充这些进步.

blocks.en: 2.2 Spatial Grounding for Robotic Manipulation
blocks.zh: 2.2 机器人操纵空间地面

blocks.en:
Spatial grounding connects visual observations with the geometric structure of the environment to support robotic manipulation.
Recent studies have incorporated explicit 3D representations into VLA policies. SpatialVLA introduces 3D positional encoding to enhance spatial awareness Qu et al. (2025) , while 3DS-VLA combines 2D-3D feature alignment with sequential spatial constraints for manipulation Li et al. (2025) .
Graph-based representations have also been explored for spatial relation modeling in navigation and autonomous driving, exemplified by BSG and GraphAD Liu et al. (2023b) ; Zhang et al. (2024) . Graph-of-Mark further enhances spatial reasoning for multimodal models via graph-based visual prompting Frisoni et al. (2026) .
blocks.zh:
空间地平面将视觉观测与环境几何结构相接,支持机器人操纵.
最近的研究将明确的三维表述纳入志愿军政策。 SpaceVLA引入了3D位置编码来增强空间意识Qu等 (2025),而3DS-VLA结合了2D-3D特征与相继的空间约束来进行操纵Li等 (2025).
还探索了导航和自主驾驶中空间关系模型的图示,BSG和GraphAD Liu等人(2023b)就是例证; 张等 (2024). Mark地图通过以图表为基础的视觉提示Frisoni等人(2026年),进一步加强了多式联运模型的空间推理。

blocks.en:
For robotic manipulation, scene graphs have been used for both high-level planning and action conditioning.
Compose by Focus employs task-relevant graphs to condition diffusion-based manipulation skills Qi et al. (2026) , while GraSP-VLA uses scene graphs for symbolic planning and policy orchestration Neau et al. (2025) .
SIR further learns task-relevant graph sparsification for action generation Mattes et al. (2026) . More directly, GraphCoT-VLA combines an updatable 3D pose-object graph with structured reasoning Huang et al. (2026) , while TriRelVLA models object-hand-task relations to condition action prediction Zhou et al. (2026) .
Other studies have explored spatiotemporal representations for manipulation: ConsisVLA-4D addresses spatiotemporal consistency Li et al. (2026) , semantic-geometric task representations jointly encode object relations and motion histories Herbert et al. (2026) , and Qian et al. maintain dynamic scene graphs as structured memory under partial observability Qian et al. (2026) .
While these studies demonstrate the value of spatial structure and temporal context, WeaveVLA focuses on explicitly encoding task-relevant relative 3D relations for action generation. A task-conditioned graph captures gripper–object and object–reference geometry, while observation-aware recurrent updates maintain pair-specific relational states across observations.

blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
WeaveVLA grounds robot actions in task-relevant relative 3D relations, as illustrated in Fig. 2 .
Given RGB observations from the available cameras, proprioception s t s_{t} , and instruction ℓ \ell , the framework associates tracked entities with visual features and estimated 3D geometry.
A task-conditioned graph organizes relative spatial relations among relevant objects, the gripper, and nearby references, while pair-specific recurrent states maintain these relations across observations.
A learned-query readout then extracts compact relational tokens from the updated graph features, which complement the original vision-language context H t H_{t} to condition a continuous action expert.

blocks.en: 3.1 Object-Centric Observation Representation
blocks.zh: 3.1 物体观察代表

blocks.en:
To ground 3D spatial relations, WeaveVLA first establishes object-centric visual representations with consistent identities across observations.
At episode initialization, an adapted YOLOE detector Wang et al. (2025) supplies labeled boxes to frozen SAM 3 Carion et al. (2026) ; Cutie Cheng et al. (2024) then propagates instance masks and identities.
Robot regions are excluded from object instance masks before feature pooling. Object appearance features are pooled from visual tokens aligned with instance masks in the same camera view, while the original VLM retains its backbone-specific camera inputs.

The gripper is represented as a separate entity. Its finger masks are obtained from robot geometry and camera calibration, and appearance features are pooled from visible finger regions using the same foreground-coverage weighting. Its 3D position is anchored at the calibrated tool center point (TCP), obtained from robot kinematics rather than visual depth.
Detector adaptation, mask filtering, and tracking details appear in Appendix E .

blocks.en: 3.2 Spatial Graph Construction and Encoding
blocks.zh: 3.2 空间图的构建和编码

blocks.en: Spatial grounding aligns geometry of tracked objects and the gripper TCP within a shared image-aligned coordinate frame. Masked metric depth from DA3Metric-Large Lin et al. (2025) is backprojected using camera intrinsics, while the calibrated TCP is transformed into the same frame. Stable references help mitigate depth-scale drift under a fixed camera, with the correction applied only to estimated object geometry. Node features combine foreground appearance, averaged VLM input embeddings of the category label, and a point MLP with max pooling over centered point clouds. Appendix B details the geometry-retention rules and graph-attention operations.

existing connections and including unmentioned objects.

blocks.en: Implementation details. We instantiate WeaveVLA on two VLA backbones, StarVLA-GR00T Community (2026) and π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} Black et al. (2025a) . The StarVLA-GR00T instantiation uses Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct Bai et al. (2025) and the QwenGR00T action framework. The relational module has a hidden width of 256 and eight attention heads, with two layers each for spatial encoding, VLM-conditioned graph propagation, and learned-query readout. We use 16 relational tokens by default. Backbone-specific training configurations and hyperparameters for each benchmark are provided in Appendix A .

blocks.en: LIBERO. LIBERO comprises four suites: Spatial, Object, Goal, and Long, with Long corresponding to LIBERO-10. We evaluate 500 rollouts per suite and report the success rate of each suite and their average.
blocks.zh: 利贝罗。 LIBERO由四个套房组成:空间套房,对象套房,目标套房和长相套房,而长相套房对应LIBERO-10. 我们评估每个套房的500套,并报告每个套房的成功率及其平均数。

blocks.en: LIBERO-Plus. LIBERO-Plus contains 10,030 perturbed tasks spanning seven perturbation categories. For each model, we reuse its LIBERO-trained checkpoint with unchanged inference settings, without additional training or fine-tuning on LIBERO-Plus. Each perturbed task is evaluated once, and overall success is pooled across all 10,030 trials. Both benchmarks use control-step limits of 220, 280, 300, and 520 for the Spatial, Object, Goal, and Long suites, respectively, with ten settling steps.
blocks.zh: 利贝罗-普卢斯。 LIBERO-Plus包含10,030个扰动任务,跨越了7个扰动类别. 对于每个模型,我们重新使用经过LIBERO训练的检查站,其推想设置不变,不对LIBERO-Plus进行额外的培训或微调. 每项令人不安的任务都经过一次评估,所有10 030起审判的总体成功率都得到汇集。 这两项基准对空间、物体、目标以及长套房分别使用220个、280个、300个和520个控制步骤限制,并有10个结算步骤。

blocks.en:
CALVIN. We evaluate WeaveVLA on CALVIN Mees et al. (2022) under the D → \rightarrow D setting, where models are trained and evaluated in environment D using separate training and evaluation sequences. The evaluation consists of 1,000 sequences of five consecutive language-conditioned subtasks, with at most 360 control steps per subtask.
We report the success rates for completing at least one through five consecutive subtasks and the average completed sequence length (Avg. Len.).
Each instruction is treated as a separate graph-state episode, with task bindings and recurrent edge states reset at each subtask transition.

我们报告至少完成一个至五个连续子任务的成功率和平均完成序列长度(Avg. Len.).
每个指令都作为单独的图态插曲处理,任务绑定和重复边缘状态重置在每个子任务过渡上.

Real-world setup. We evaluate three real-world manipulation tasks as shown in Fig. 3 . 1) Bowl Stacking. The robot places the first bowl on a plate, then uses its position to align and stack the second bowl. 2) Place Pens in Cups. The robot sequentially picks up two pens and places each in its designated cup. 3) Clean Table. The robot hangs the mug on the rack, then places the first paper ball, the block, and the second paper ball in the basket.
For each task and method, we conduct 30 trials under standard conditions and 30 out-of-distribution (OOD) trials, evenly split across table clutter, lighting perturbations, and background variations. We report binary task success and a stage-wise progress score based on completed stages in the predefined task sequence. Appendix G provides detailed task configurations, OOD settings, and progress scoring criteria.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We have introduced WeaveVLA, a framework that enhances VLA models by explicitly encoding task-relevant relative 3D relations and modeling their evolution throughout manipulation.
By combining task-conditioned sparse graph construction with pair-specific recurrent relational updating, WeaveVLA integrates current spatial geometry and historical relational context for continuous action generation.
Extensive evaluations on simulation benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements across different VLA backbones, highlighting the effectiveness of explicit relational grounding for robotic manipulation.
On three real-world tasks, WeaveVLA improves success over both baselines under standard and perturbed conditions.
blocks.zh:
我们引入了WeaveVLA,这个框架通过明确编码与任务相关的相对3D关系,并在整个操纵过程中模拟其演化过程来增强VLA模型.
通过将任务条件化的稀有图构造与对偶的经常性关系更新相结合,WeaveVLA整合了当前空间几何和历史关系背景,用于持续行动生成.
对模拟基准的广泛评价表明,不同甚高频系统的主干网不断得到改进,突出了为机器人操纵而建立明确关系的有效性。
在三个现实世界的任务中,织女VLA在标准条件下和扰动条件下都提高了基线的成功率.

blocks.en: Appendix A Training Configuration
blocks.zh: 附录A 培训配置

blocks.en: Table 6 summarizes the training configurations of WeaveVLA with StarVLA and π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} backbones. On LIBERO, both variants use the same demonstration set. For CALVIN D → \rightarrow D, both variants train on the training split of environment D. For all three real-world tasks, WeaveVLA uses the StarVLA-GR00T backbone and predicts absolute joint configurations from real-world demonstrations. For all three real-world tasks, the VLM receives four synchronized RGB views from the third-person camera, the high-mounted main camera, and both wrist cameras. We construct the graph from the third-person view and pool node appearance features from VLM tokens aligned with the instance masks in that view.
